effect_size.excerpt: The highest category of serum concentrations for several forms of vitamin A and E were significantly and positively associated with prostate cancer risk, including retinol (OR = 6.08), lutein (OR = 2.07), α-carotene (OR = 3.27), β-carotene (OR = 3.04), ubiquinone (OR = 2.44), α-tocopherol (OR = 2.40), δ-tocotrienol (OR = 3.70), γ-tocotrienol (OR = 3.02), and α-tocotrienol (OR = 2.76), compared with the lowest category.

comparison.excerpt: In all our analyses, the lowest micronutrient category was taken as the referent.

ethnicity.excerpt: The controls were frequency-matched to cases based on 5-year age groups and ethnicity.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test was not performed because fewer than 10 studies were available. With a small number of studies, the test generally has insufficient power to reliably detect funnel plot asymmetry.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 3 studies yielded an effect size of 1.19 (95% CI: 0.79–1.79), indicating no statistically significant association between coenzyme q10 and prostate cancer\aggressive. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by substantial heterogeneity (I² = 69.43%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
